subject: tu:game/game/gamemain
value: THE gGameMode RESPELLING CAMPAIGN IS NOW FULLY CLOSED. A project-wide sweep of src/ finds ZERO `gGameMode <cmp> literal`, case arm, assignment, arithmetic operand, OR family-bit mask remaining, in any base. THE FAMILY-BIT MASKS ARE RESOLVED, reversing v2's settled position that they must stay raw. v2 held that `gGameMode & 0x8000` / `& 0x4000` could not be truthfully spelled because no single mode constant names a family -- correct as far as it went, but it treated 'no mode constant fits' as 'no name exists'. The right name was not a mode at all but a MASK, and the enum supports one exactly. DERIVATION, verdict CLEAN with no exceptions: partitioning all 49 e_mode constants by high bit is disjoint and total -- 0x8000 set on exactly the 11 MA_* ids (base 0..10), 0x4000 on exactly the 13 MG_* ids (base 11..23), neither on exactly the 25 bare M_* ids (0..24), BOTH on no constant; and because the two families' base ranges do not overlap and the largest bare M_* is 24 (0x18), each mask selects one whole family and can never alias a bare id. Verified verbatim against the Xbox PDB enum e_mode (research/xbox_symbols/misc.h:16779-16830). The NAMES come from the enum's own prefixes (MA_ = attract, MG_ = game), so they assert nothing the vocabulary does not already assert. All 20 use sites were read and every one agrees; three are individually decisive -- gamemain.c:4079 tests the mask INSIDE the attract-loop switch (the MA_FLYBY arm, at a label named attract_tail); gauntworld.c:6585 writes `(gGameMode & 0x8000) && gGameMode != MA_DEMO && gGameMode != MA_INSTRUCT`, excluding two MA_* ids from the set the mask selects; screensaver.c:776 ORs the mask with two specific MG_* ids. include/game/gamemode.h now defines MODE_GROUP_ATTRACT 0x8000 and MODE_GROUP_GAME 0x4000 with the derivation in a comment. Spelled as MACROS, not enumerators, for two reasons worth reusing: an enumerator would assert the masks are modes (they are not), and a macro expanding to the identical literal token makes byte-identity hold by CONSTRUCTION -- the post-preprocessor token stream is character-for-character unchanged -- rather than by the constant-folding argument wave 3 relied on. 20 sites converted across 8 TUs, all byte-identical: gamemain.c 8 (1280/1834/3577/3944/3978/4079/4900/4976), player.c 4 (716/861/1319/3257), gauntworld.c 3 (1610/5059/6585), and one each in items.c (1256), combat.c (2253), message.c (724), screensaver.c (776), sndfx.c (the sndFxPaused() macro). v2's site count of ~15 was low; the true figure is 20. THE sndfx.c IDENTITY ANOMALY IS RESOLVED, AND v2's PREMISE FOR IT IS NOW STALE. v1 and v2 both held sndfx.c out on the grounds that `sndFxInit assigns a POINTER into gGameMode (sndfx.c:217, gGameMode = (s32)a where a is a void* parameter)`, contradicting sndFxPaused()'s use of it as a mode, and demanded the identity be settled before any respelling. In the current tree that assignment reads `gGameMode = mode;` inside `void sndFxInit(s32 mode, s32 wave)` -- an s32 mode id, no pointer and no cast anywhere. The audio lane that owned the TU during wave 3 evidently recovered the real signature. There is no contradiction left and the symbol is the ordinary mode global; sndfx.c was converted normally and gained `#include "game/gamemode.h"` (it had declared its own extern). Any future reader of v1/v2 should disregard the pointer-assignment claim. STILL DELIBERATELY UNTOUCHED, and this is a hard rule rather than an omission: sndfx.c:555's `| 0x8000` is an UNRELATED voice-handle flag on a different variable and must NEVER be respelled as a mode-group mask. THE screensaver.c TYPE DIVERGENCE IS A CAP, NOT A PENDING CHORE -- v2(iii)'s framing of it as merely 'outside wave 3's scope' is corrected. `extern int gGameMode` at screensaver.c:117 CANNOT be harmonized to s32 byte-identically: the change alone regressed ScreenSaver real 52 -> 64, a pure reorder of one 4-instruction loop preheader with an IDENTICAL opcode multiset at equal insn counts (defake_gate reports CONFLICT, not REGRESSION -- a pass that accepts CONFLICT would bank the loss silently). Reverted; the divergence is kept and now documented in place with a source comment. See attempt.screensaver-ggamemode-extern-type.20260831.v1 and claim.law.int-vs-signed-long-extern-reorders-schedule.20260831.v1, which also records the same fix succeeding byte-identically in message.c -- so the hazard is per-site, not per-symbol. GENERAL LESSON FOR FUTURE VOCABULARY SWEEPS, beyond this enum: when a site resists naming because no member of the vocabulary fits it, check whether the site is testing a PROPERTY OF the vocabulary rather than comparing against a member. A family/group mask, a range predicate, or a validity test needs a name from a different namespace than the members themselves, and refusing to name it at all -- as waves 1-3 did here for four rounds -- leaves real debt behind a reasonable-sounding argument.
